meta.description: Test whether a GWAS signal and a molecular QTL (eQTL/sQTL/pQTL/mQTL) share the same causal variant -- e.g. "does my GWAS lead SNP colocalize with this eQTL, or is it just LD" -- using Bayesian colocalization (coloc.abf, coloc.susie, HyPrColoc, moloc, eCAVIAR, SMR/HEIDI, PWCoCo, SharePro). Use when integrating GWAS with eQTL/sQTL/pQTL/mQTL, distinguishing shared causal variants from LD-driven coincidence, handling allelic heterogeneity, choosing between single-causal vs multi-causal methods, picking PP.H4 thresholds, running sensitivity over p12, or harmonising summary statistics for colocalization.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 7 re-audit datasets are freshly generated and explicitly labelled synthetic/planted-truth (independent seeds/parameters from both the pre-fix audit and the fixer's own scratch scripts). No fabricated DOI/PMID, trial results, sample sizes, or p-values presented as real.

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-genomics / statistical-genetics research tooling only; no output makes an individual diagnostic or prescriptive claim.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found. One real precision gap remains in the revised PP.H3-inflation trigger text (see Input 6, P1 recommendation): the fix correctly added a power/effect-size clause, but independent testing shows the specific 'limited power' condition as currently worded does not reliably produce the claimed PP.H3-dominant symptom (H1 dominates instead in both tested power regimes). This is a documentation-precision gap, not a fallacy: no output inverts a causal conclusion.

code_usability.detail: Both previously-crashing coloc.susie example files (examples/coloc_susie.R, examples/coloc_susie_multicausal.R) were re-run byte-for-byte, unmodified, from the fork, and both completed cleanly with exact planted-truth recovery -- the P0 defect from the pre-fix audit is confirmed gone, independently, not on the fixer's word. All other executed code (coloc.abf pipeline, flag_excluded_region() gate, harmonise(), the real SMR 1.3.1 + plink2 CLI pipeline) ran without syntax errors, missing dependencies, or crashes across all 7 inputs.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness and appropriateness remain 4/4 each (broad, accurate 8-method coverage with a clear decision tree, unchanged from pre-fix). Correctness improves from 2/4 to 3/4: both P0 example crashes are independently confirmed fixed (Inputs 2-3), and the PP.H3-inflation trigger text was rewritten with the missing power/effect-size clause -- but a new independent test (Input 6) shows that clause is not yet empirically well-calibrated (H1, not PP.H3, dominates under the documented 'limited power' condition), so correctness is not yet a clean 4/4.

recommendations.title: Revised PP.H3-inflation trigger condition is not yet empirically calibrated
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's fixed trigger text requires r2~0.3-0.6 AND 'comparable effect sizes / limited power' for PP.H3 inflation. Independent testing at r2=0.505 with comparable effect sizes and two different reduced-power eQTL sample sizes (N=150 and N=400) shows PP.H1 (GWAS-only), not PP.H3, dominates in both cases; PP.H3 stayed below 0.05 throughout.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix's own re-verification tested the well-powered end of the claim (proving r2 alone is insufficient) but did not test the newly-added 'limited power' condition itself, so that clause is unverified and, on this evidence, does not reliably produce the claimed symptom.
recommendations.fix: Run a calibration sweep over eQTL N (e.g. 200, 400, 700, 1000, 5000) at fixed r2~0.5 and comparable effect sizes to find the actual regime (if any) where PP.H3 dominates rather than PP.H1, and replace 'comparable effect sizes / limited power' with the empirically-identified band, or reframe the mechanism qualitatively instead of naming a specific power condition that does not hold up.

recommendations.title: harmonise() has no strand-complement-flip branch and no pitfall callout for it
recommendations.problem: A SNP pair coded on opposite strands without being palindromic (e.g. A/G vs its complement T/C) is neither 'same' nor 'flip' under harmonise()'s literal definition and is silently dropped. None of the five 'Harmonisation pitfalls to watch for' bullets mention this case (they cover build mismatch and palindromic-at-high-MAF only).
recommendations.root_cause: harmonise() implements only an allele-order-swap check, not a strand-complement check, and the pitfalls list was not updated to reflect this scope limit when the function moved from usage-guide.md into SKILL.md this fix pass.
recommendations.fix: Add a sixth pitfall bullet documenting that harmonise() does not resolve non-palindromic strand mismatches and that upstream strand-harmonization is required before calling it, or extend the function with a complement-check branch if silent SNP loss at scale is a concern.
